mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace an Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI engine typically ranges from £4,000 to £6,500 for a rebuilt unit, depending on whether it is a TDI or TFSI variant.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of turbo oil strainer failure in an Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a distinct metallic "death rattle" from the turbochargers on startup or under load, illuminated oil pressure warnings, and eventual loss of power.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the vehicle is in good overall condition and valued above £10,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a highly cost-effective alternative to buying a new premium Sportback.

mainEntity.name: Does the replacement engine include quattro and ECU calibration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, any professional supply & fit service for the Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI must include ODIS coding to ensure the engine ECU communicates correctly with the quattro transfer case and S tronic transmission.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CDUD and CRTD engine codes in the Audi A7?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CDUD is the 3.0L V6 TDI (245hp) used in early-to-mid 4G models (2012-2016), while the CRTD is the updated 3.0L V6 TDI (272hp) introduced for late 4G and 4K models (2015-2018) with Euro 6 compliance and AdBlue systems.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: While the S7 badge is globally renowned for its 4.0 TFSI V8, this variant page covers the high-performance 3.0L V6 architectures (both TDI and TFSI) that share the Sportback chassis, frequently searched by enthusiasts and owners of high-spec A7/S7 models seeking precise engine matching.

milestones.description: CTSA, 3.0L V6 TFSI Supercharged (300hp), introduced in the 4G generation, offering robust torque and refined petrol performance.
CDUD, 3.0L V6 TDI (245hp), the dominant high-torque diesel variant for the 4G chassis, favoured for its towing capacity and motorway efficiency.
CRTD, 3.0L V6 TDI (272hp), introduced for the late 4G and early 4K generations, featuring updated Euro 6 emissions controls and AdBlue systems.
CREC, 3.0L V6 TFSI Supercharged (333hp), carried forward with refined engine management, improved supercharger mapping, and enhanced reliability.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI is a highly capable premium Sportback, but its complex V6 architecture introduces specific failure points across the 4G and 4K generations. The CDUD/CRTD (diesel) and CTSA/CREC (petrol) engine codes dominate replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Oil Strainer Failure - Why the Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI (CDUD/CRTD) Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI (CDUD, CRTD, 2012-2018)
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger oil feed strainer can become blocked with debris, restricting oil flow to the turbo and top end. This triggers a "death rattle" from the turbos and can lead to catastrophic oil starvation and engine seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil strainer, inspect/replace turbochargers, flush oil system
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as a preventative or early-stage repair

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if oil starvation has caused catastrophic bearing or block damage

problems.recommendation: For the 3.0 TDI, address any turbo rattle or oil pressure warnings immediately. A £1,500 specialist strainer and turbo service is a minor expense compared to a £5,000+ full engine replacement caused by oil starvation. For the 3.0 TFSI, a rebuilt engine assembly with an updated supercharger coupler and revised cooling components is the most reliable long-term solution to restore factory performance.

problems.h4: Supercharger Coupler & Cooling Leaks - Why the Audi A7 S7 3.0 TFSI (CTSA/CREC) Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Audi A7 S7 3.0 TDI / TFSI (CTSA, CREC, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: The internal supercharger coupler wears out, causing a distinct rattling noise and loss of boost. This is often compounded by brittle plastic coolant crossover pipes in the V of the engine that crack and leak.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace supercharger snout/coupler and plastic coolant pipes
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended to prevent overheating and restore performance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when overheating has caused head gasket failure or internal damage
